text:
maria: FYI - new model intake: community fork 'Marlin-13B' landed in model-registry. model card attached says weights licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, but the training data provenance is fuzzy. want to run quantization/latency bench for Dedicated offering. can we proceed with host/dedicated/private?

stella: quick q — CC BY-NC-ND forbids derivatives and commercial use, right? ND = no derivatives so quantized weights might count as derivative?

maria: exactly my concern. also the repo has a short clause: "no redistribution of the checkpoint binaries without express permission". link: https://git.example/marlin/blob/main/LICENSE

license-bot: license-detected: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0. flagged: redistribution_prohibited, commercial_use_prohibited, derivatives_restricted. recommend legal review.

tj: lane-in from legal — CC BY-NC-ND is tricky. ND means you may not distribute modified versions. Quantization could be interpreted as a transformation (derivative). Hosting a model behind an API is arguably "making available" the model (redistribution-like). Commercial restriction blocks paid hosting. we need clarifications from upstream authors before hosted/paid offerings.

eli: product perspective: customers will ask if they can use the model in production. if license is NC we can't offer it under paid hosted tiers. Dedicated/reserved private deployments that the customer self-hosts might be okay if we avoid redistributing the weights. but we need clear guidance.

sam: security/compliance angle — also check export-control flags. model registry scan didn't raise EAR-violations, but provenance unknown. if there are proprietary datasets, downstream reuse could trigger IP claims. recommend staging-only experiments in our air-gapped sandbox (Private) until legal signs off.

stella: what about serving quantized weights generated on our infra but not distributing the checkpoint files? e.g., we keep quantization artifacts inside the inference runtime and only expose outputs. is that permitted?

tj: that’s a gray area. important distinction: creating a quantized binary and then distributing that binary is distribution. Running quantization as a one-off transformation to serve results from our runtime without exposing weights can still violate ND if the license treats the served model as a published derivative. precedent varies. we should not assume.

maria: propose immediate actions: 1) pause hosted offering; 2) run offline quantization experiments in Private sandbox (no checkout beyond engineering team); 3) open formal license clarification with upstream authors; 4) add to onboarding checklist: license clause + allowed transformations + redistribution policy + commercial use allowlist.

eli: +1. also add a product note: if authors approve "private-hosting-only" we can enable it as a Dedicated/Private-only model in the console with clear label.

tj: i'll draft an email template to request permissions. include exact asks: permission to (a) perform quantization for serving, (b) host quantized binaries under Redwood-managed private deployments, (c) offer paid hosted inference. include a timeline and CYA attribution requirement.

sam: i'll add a ticket to infra: create an isolated experiment pool (no checkpoint export, limited access, audit logs). label: MARLIN-licensing-sandbox.

maria: putting minimal license excerpt here for context:
```
You are free to: Share — copy and redistribute the material in any medium or format.
Under the following terms:
– Attribution — You must give appropriate credit.
– NonCommercial — You may not use the material for commercial purposes.
– NoDerivatives — If you remix, transform, or build upon the material, you may not distribute the modified material.
```

stella: ok. last question: embeddings/outputs — even if weights have NC/ND, are outputs (text/embeddings) considered derivative? some licensors treat generated outputs as allowed, others not. we need explicit permission for downstream output usage by paying customers.

tj: right. request should include permission for commercial use of model outputs and embeddings. otherwise we must restrict outputs to non-commercial customers and internal evals.

maria: i've created the intake doc update (link internal): https://redwood.internal/onboarding/marlin-intake — note: flagged for Legal review.

eli: can we add a short banner in model-catalog UI for "license pending: limited use" so customers don't mistakenly use it?

maria: yes i'll flag it.

tj: follow-up: i'll send the upstream email today and post updates here. if authors are unresponsive after 7 days we'll mark "ineligible for hosted" and allow only Private deploys under strict contract terms.

sam: noted. infra ticket created: MARLIN-2345 (sandbox), assigned to infra-qa.

stella: thanks — will also run a small eval to compare quantized perf in the sandbox, but will not persist or export any artifacts until legal confirms.

maria: action items summary: tj -> contact authors (email + ask list), sam -> sandbox ticket + access controls, eli -> product labeling + restrict in UI, stella -> ephemeral quantization evals, maria -> update ingestion doc & block hosted until cleared. tagging for follow-up in 7d. :calendar: 

eli: :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all. keeping thread for audit trail.

license-bot: note added to registry: license_pending_contact (1841005432).
